title: SEAD · mission sequence
subtitle: ISR, stimulation, strike and follow-through
description: A source-structured visualization of the Mitchell Institute SEAD concept, expanded into a system-of-systems view using documented platform roles and illustrative mission relationships.

citations.locator: Figure 9; SEAD phases across the 24-hour presentation period

assumptions: Phase names follow the report's conceptual SEAD sequence; displayed geography, timing, actor counts and routes remain editorial illustration.
Platform roles are documented separately from the illustrative mission package.
No sensor, weapon, threat, targeting, kill-chain performance or engagement outcome is modeled.
Relationship lines explain support, data, electronic-attack and teaming functions; they do not assert classified interfaces.

phases.title: Continuous ISR
phases.narrative: Persistent ISR and battle-space awareness form the information layer supporting the SEAD concept.

phases.title: Stimulate / Decoy / Jam
phases.narrative: CCA and electronic-attack effects are shown as separate but cooperating mission functions.

phases.title: Strike SAGs
phases.narrative: Crewed and uncrewed strike-support elements enter the same mission package; no engagement outcome is calculated.

phases.title: Harass / EA
phases.narrative: Electronic attack and uncrewed pressure remain active after the primary strike phase.

phases.title: Harass & BDA
phases.narrative: ISR and follow-through effects remain visible to emphasize the mission as an information and effects network rather than a single aircraft action.

actors.label: ISR element
actors.role: Near-real-time intelligence collection and dissemination research role

actors.label: CCA SEAD element
actors.role: Abstract CCA element representing stimulation, electronic attack and strike support
